title: Prospectivity Multiplexer: field probes for model-bundle price/latency tradeoffs
creator: Priya Raman
description: Run a focused market research + field probe to quantify how mid-market and enterprise buyers trade off bundled model pricing versus latency SLOs. The goal is to produce an actionable recommendation for product packaging (hosted token bundles, reserved bursts, ded + fallback routing) and a set of signal thresholds that trigger sales/ops playbooks.
hypothesis: There exists a segment of PLG-to-midmarket customers (billing $1k-$20k monthly) who will accept a <20% latency degradation in exchange for a 25%+ unit-cost reduction if the platform offers predictable fallback bundling and transparent quality SLAs.
research_plan: 1) Synthesize competitive bundle pricing: collect published and field-reported bundle prices from 6 providers across NA/EU/APAC.

2) Instrument synthetic workloads: create 4 representative enterprise prompts (RAG retrieval, summarization, multi-step chat, embeddings-heavy indexing) and run latency/cost sweeps across model variants and quantization profiles.

3) Field probes with 8 customers: run 2-week A/B toggles for customers willing to trial a bundled fallback policy that trades model variant for cost (with explicit consent and rollback). Capture qualitative sales feedback.
4) Build decision canvas: map observable signals (QPS, cold-start frequency, token mix) to recommended bundle types and trigger points for sales to propose dedicated vs hosted options.
5) Deliver artifacts: cost-latency curves, sample messaging for sales, runbook for SRE on safe rollback and monitoring thresholds.
decisions: Use synthetic workloads aligned to customer telemetry rather than only public benchmarks — decided 2025-03-16 after PM+SRE review.
Prioritize 3 bundle prototypes: token-bucket hosted, reserved-dedicated micro-commit, and transparent fallback routing with quality SLAs.
Instrument billing delta visibility at token-level in the dashboard before running field probes (SRE dependency agreed).
tradeoffs: Accuracy vs unit-cost: quantized model variants may drop quality on edge cases; include evaluation prompt set for regressions.
Operational complexity: reserved-dedicated offers predictable throughput but increases provisioning inertia; recommend micro-commit sizes to mitigate.
Sales friction vs clarity: exposing too many bundle permutations confuses procurement; limit prototypes to three clear offerings.
Privacy/regulatory: field probes must avoid shipping PII to external model providers; for customers requiring privacy we will use Private deployment testbeds only.
